title: Decode Pathway Efficiency - sparse vs prefetch (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a short executive-sketch style benchmark exploring decode-pathway efficiency tradeoffs between a sparse-batching execution path (sparsebatch) and a predictive prefetch/tiling path (prefetch). Goal: produce a concise summary suitable for a console one-pager and to surface concrete knobs for the Optimize product team.

Background and motivation:
- Recent customer incidents show p95 degradation during 10-20s microbursts even when p50 remains fine. Suspected cause: decode kernel under-utilization + KV cache miss amplification when switching execution paths.
- Two promising mitigations evaluated: sparsebatch (compact scheduling to keep occupancy high for short sequences) and prefetch (proactive loading of KV/weights based on prefix heuristics). Both have different cost/latency profiles.

Experiment setup (short):
- Model: 13B transformer (causal), standard Redwood runtime baseline (float16).
- Hardware: 1xA100-80GB equivalent, isolated instance (no noisy neighbors).
- Workloads: synthetic sessionized mix: 70% short-turn (<=32 tokens), 20% medium (33-128), 10% long (>128). Microburst scenarios: 100 reqs/sec sustained for 10s; steady-state: 20 reqs/sec.
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p95 latency (ms), tokens/sec throughput, estimated $/M tokens (amortized infra cost), GPU occupancy, KV cache hitrate.
- Configs compared:
  A) baseline (multiplexing + default batching)
  B) sparsebatch enabled (tight slot packing + short-session priority)
  C) prefetch enabled (predictive KV pre-load and peek-tiling)
  D) hybrid (sparsebatch + conservative prefetch)

Raw (median of 5 runs) results table (ascii):

Config        | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p95(ms) | tokens/s | $/M tokens | KV hitrate | GPU occ%
--------------|---------|---------|---------|----------|------------|------------|--------
Baseline      | 42      | 210     | 480     | 18,400   | 1.00       | 0.62       | 48
Sparsebatch   | 46      | 150     | 260     | 22,300   | 0.88       | 0.65       | 72
Prefetch      | 38      | 170     | 300     | 20,800   | 0.95       | 0.79       | 60
Hybrid        | 40      | 130     | 210     | 23,100   | 0.86       | 0.78       | 74

Interpretation (quick):
- Sparsebatch improves throughput (+21%) and drops p95 substantially vs baseline in microburst because higher GPU occupancy (72% vs 48%). Cost per token falls ~12%. However p50 increases slightly due to scheduling overheads for very short requests.
- Prefetch improves KV hitrate from 0.62 to 0.79, lowering p50 and p90; p95 improves vs baseline but not as much as sparsebatch in the worst tail. Prefetch carries some infrastructure cost (prefetch bandwidth and extra memory pressure) so $/M tokens is slightly higher than sparsebatch.
- Hybrid combines the strengths: best throughput, best p95 in our runs, slightly higher memory/KV footprint but still cheaper than baseline when amortized.

Representative ASCII latency distribution sketch (pctl vs ms):
- Baseline:  p50=42 | p90~210 | p95~480  (heavy long tail)
- Sparsebatch: p50=46 | p90~150 | p95~260 (compressed tail, shift right at p50)
- Prefetch: p50=38 | p90~170 | p95~300 (lower center, moderate tail)

Operational notes and caveats:
- Synthetic mix approximates real conversational traffic but real customers show higher variance in prefix reuse; prefetch may do better in workloads with strong locality.
- Sparsebatch scheduling increases request coalescing which may harm ultra-low-latency singletons (games, high frequency trading-like workloads). Consider exposing a per-route knob to disable sparsebatch.
- Prefetch relies on accurate prefix heuristics; mispredictions increase unnecessary KV churn and transient memory pressure. We used a conservative predictor in these runs.
- GPU occupancy measurements are runtime-observed; need kernel-level traces to confirm where cycles are spent (decode vs memory-copy).

Short recommendations (for console/Optimize UI):
1) Expose an "aggressive burst" profile that enables sparsebatch + conservative prefetch (default for burst-tolerant routes).
2) Add a per-route estimator card showing expected p95 and $/M tokens delta for enabling each knob (simulate with offline mixing tool).
3) Instrument and ship a small kernel tracing job to collect decode vs memcpy split — will inform further optimizations on sparsebatch overhead.
4) Add a runtime experiment: rollout hybrid to 10% of production traffic on Dedicated to validate at scale (Jira: ENG-4823).

Next steps / TODOs (actionable):
- [ ] Run same experiment on 2xA100 (multi-GPU) to confirm scaling of sparsebatch.
- [ ] Repeat with 70/30 workload skew (more short turns) to measure p50 hit rate.
- [ ] Surface a simple cost calculator widget in the Console showing $/M tokens delta for each profile.
- [ ] Author a short customer-facing note summarizing tradeoffs for PLG docs (1 page).

Notes to reviewers: want feedback on whether we should prioritize prefetch investment (complex but good for locality) vs sparsebatch (lower complexity, big tail wins). Also thinking about adding a third axis (energy/power) for customers with edge deployments.

Quick provenance: run artifacts + csvs attached in GH PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1297), tracker: ENG-4823, reference design doc: confluence link above.

-- Maya
